plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Self-serve pay-as-you-go account, no platform fee; GPU quota may need a request.

caveats: Use rates BEFORE October 1, 2026. Pricing landing spot floors differ materially from documented preemptible rates: both retained but not conflated. L40S separately bills CPU/RAM; other GPU platform reference bundles include them. Dynamic spot starts October 8, not September 22 announcement date. As of Sep 28 docs fixed preemptible prices still apply.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

B300/B200/H200/H100 on-demand prices rise 2026-10-01 to $9.50/$8.50/$5.40/$4.50 per GPU-h (from $7.85/$7.15/$4.50/$3.85); RTX PRO 6000 and L40S unchanged. Spot prices are dynamic (from $0.79) and left unpriced.

CPU-only VMs (cpu-d3 AMD Genoa all regions, cpu-e2 Intel Ice Lake eu-north1) added 2026-09-28 at pre-October rates $0.012/vCPU-h + $0.0032/GiB-h; from 2026-10-01 AMD becomes $0.015 + $0.0045 and Intel $0.012 + $0.0045 (nebius.com/prices landing: "from $0.10" -> "from $0.13" AMD, "$0.05" -> "$0.06" Intel). Plain VMs: no sandbox API, disk ($0.071/GiB-month network SSD) billed separately.

Serverless AI (Devlabs, jobs, endpoints: container workloads on Compute VMs) has no own pricing; it bills Compute VM + disk rates and counts toward Compute quotas. A stopped Devlab still pays its whole container disk.

Preemptible: fixed prices ($2.15 H100, $2.45 H200, $3.95 B200, $4.30 B300, $0.95 RTX PRO 6000) apply until 2026-10-07; from 2026-10-08 a dynamic spot price updated every 15 min, floor 'from $0.79' (H100/H200/RTX) / 'from $0.99' (B200/B300), ceiling one cent below on-demand. L40S preemptible stays flat ($0.65 GPU + CPU/RAM). Spot modes remain unpriced.
Commitment discounts: up to 35% below on-demand for multi-month reservations of large clusters (prepaid, sales, company accounts); rates unpublished.

fleet.tiers: Default GPU quotas (regular VMs, per region): H100 32 (eu-north1); H200 32 eu-north1, 8 eu-west1, 0 us-central1; B200 0 (us-central1, me-west1); B300 32 (uk-south1, eu-west2, us-north1); RTX PRO 6000 32 (uk-south2, eu-south1), 0 us-central1; L40S 2 (eu-north1). 12 regular + 8 preemptible GPU VMs per region.
fleet.notes: No single current aggregate GPU quota asserted: historical published per-type allowances are not additive and current project/region quota must be checked. Blog describes quota approval friction; no standard review time.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Compute preserves all data on the volumes attached to a stopped preemptible VM.
snapshot_auto.note: Plain KVM VMs: stop (or preemption) keeps attached disks (persistent_disk) but takes no state snapshot and memory is lost; no snapshot schedules/policies found in docs (llms-full grep).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: To create a snapshot, you don't need to stop a virtual machine.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk snapshots (console/CLI/Go/Python/JS SDK/Terraform compute_v1_disk_snapshot) of boot and additional disks, running or stopped; restore = create a new disk from the snapshot, so new VMs can boot from it (also custom boot images from disks). Disk only, no memory; project-scoped; billed separately.

harness_api.note: GPU/CPU IaaS cloud (Compute VMs, Managed K8s, Soperator, Serverless AI jobs/endpoints/Devlabs); no agent-harness product or API in the docs index. Driving agents would be DIY over SSH/exec.

egress_allowlist.quote: each security rule describes whether ingress or egress traffic with certain parameters (source, destination, protocol) should be allowed or denied.
egress_allowlist.note: VPC security groups on the VM network interface: ALLOW/DENY egress by destination CIDR (up to 8), ports, protocol TCP/UDP/ICMP/ANY, or destination security group; unmatched traffic is denied, so default-deny is possible. Default SG allows all. No hostname/FQDN rules.

egress_http_rules.quote: controlling ingress and egress traffic at the packet level
egress_http_rules.note: Security rules are L3/L4 only (CIDR/port/protocol); no L7 method/path/header filtering documented.

ingress_rules.quote: You can specify a security group as the source for an ingress security rule
ingress_rules.note: Security-group ingress rules by source CIDR/port/protocol/SG; public IPv4 is optional per VM (private-only VMs possible, reachable via Nebius Tunnels).

guest_firewall.note: Full KVM VMs with root and own kernel; iptables/nftables inside the guest work as on any Linux VM.

secret_proxy.quote: A service account associated with the given VM launches the script and retrieves the secret with the API key.
secret_proxy.note: SecretStash (formerly MysteryBox) is a secret store: secrets are fetched into the VM or injected as env vars (Serverless AI jobs/endpoints); no credential-injecting egress proxy.

volume_attach.quote: One Compute network SSD disk can only be added to one running VM at a time.
volume_attach.note: Additional network SSD disks (SSD, SSD Non-replicated, SSD IO M3), standalone and reattachable; plus shared filesystems. Attach mode READ_WRITE.

volume_shared.quote: One shared filesystem can be attached to multiple VMs at once.
volume_shared.note: Shared filesystems mounted via virtiofs, same-project only, attach_mode READ_WRITE ('The only supported value is `READ_WRITE`'); can also be exposed as S3 via filesystem buckets. Network disks are single-attach.

isolation.quote: When a VM is `Stopping`, its hypervisor shuts down the operating system of this VM.
isolation.note: Standard IaaS full-VM product (Compute VMs with own kernel, root, GRUB/pvpanic guest tuning). Docs confirm a hypervisor boundary but do not name QEMU/KVM explicitly; qemu-kvm is the standard technology for this class of Linux cloud VM and is the best-supported value.

image_oci.quote: A container virtual machine (VM) is a VM with a container image deployed. You can use containers provided by Nebius AI Cloud or containers with custom Docker images from public registries.
image_oci.note: Container VMs can be created directly from a custom Docker image pulled from a public registry.

desktop.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — IaaS GPU/CPU VM cloud, no managed graphical desktop/VNC/RDP product (only a text-only serial console).

browser.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no managed/real browser product; a user could install one themselves inside a VM but that is not a shipped feature.

computer_use.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — plain GPU/CPU IaaS, no screenshot/click computer-use API.

anti_bot.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — IaaS GPU/CPU cloud, no stealth/anti-fingerprinting product.

captcha_solving.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — GPU/CPU IaaS VM product, not a scraping/automation service.

egress_ip_type.quote: How to enable a public IP address for a VM
egress_ip_type.note: Public/static IPv4 addresses are allocated from Nebius' own datacenter IP pools (VPC allocations); no residential/mobile IP offering exists.

fork.quote: A disk snapshot captures a point-in-time copy of a disk. This is an instant disk backup that allows you to: Clone and recover a certain state of the disk.
fork.note: A disk snapshot (or a custom image) can be used as the boot disk source for one or many new VMs, effectively cloning a machine's disk state into new machines.

fork_running.quote: To create a snapshot, you don't need to stop a virtual machine.
fork_running.note: Disk snapshots can be taken from a running VM's disk without stopping it, and new VMs can then be booted from that snapshot/image.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A disk snapshot captures a point-in-time copy of a disk.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots/clones are disk-only; memory state and running processes are not captured, so a cloned VM boots fresh rather than resuming running processes.

pause_resume.quote: You are charged for computing resources (GPUs, vCPUs, RAM) of running virtual machines (VMs). Computing resources of stopped VMs are not charged (this does not apply to storage volumes...)
pause_resume.note: Stopping a VM releases/pauses compute billing (GPU/vCPU/RAM) while disks continue to be billed separately; the VM can later be started again with its disk state intact.

wake_on_request.quote: How to stop and start VMs manually
wake_on_request.note: VMs are stopped/started manually (or via autohealing on maintenance events); no mechanism found that wakes a stopped VM automatically when a network request arrives.

auto_stop_idle.quote: You can create a VM with the autohealing function. It allows a VM to automatically stop and start each time maintenance is scheduled.
auto_stop_idle.note: Automatic stop/start is tied to maintenance/autohealing and preemptible eviction, not to workload idleness; no idle-based auto-stop feature documented.

live_resize.quote: Compute supports hot resize: the resize operation itself does not require stopping the VM. However, you need to restart the VM afterward for the operating system to recognize the new disk size.
live_resize.note: Only disk capacity supports hot resize (and still needs an OS restart to take effect); no documented way to change a VM's vCPU/RAM (platform/preset) on a running instance without recreating/replacing it.

agent_harnesses.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no coding-agent (Claude Code/Codex/etc.) templates or preinstalled harnesses; only application container images like Jupyter Notebook.

own_agent_api.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — GPU/CPU IaaS cloud, no first-party browser/computer-use/research task-agent product or API.

mcp_server.quote: The Nebius docs Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives any MCP-compatible AI tool a direct connection to the Nebius documentation.
mcp_server.note: Nebius's only MCP server is for searching/reading its documentation; there is no MCP server to create/control Compute VMs or sandboxes.

lang_python.quote: Nebius AI Cloud provides public boot disk images for GPU and non-GPU VMs.
lang_python.note: Default public images are Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (with/without CUDA), which ships python3 out of the box; not a managed 'runtime' feature but present on the standard image.

lang_node.quote: Nebius AI Cloud provides public boot disk images for GPU and non-GPU VMs.
lang_node.note: Public images are plain Ubuntu; Node.js is not part of the base image (only python3 ships by default) and must be installed manually.

inbound_https.quote: How to enable a public IP address for a VM
inbound_https.note: Every VM can get a public IPv4 address with no provider-side port restriction on 443, so operators can terminate HTTPS themselves; there is no managed HTTPS-URL/reverse-proxy feature, but inbound HTTPS traffic to the machine is possible.

windows.quote: Nebius AI Cloud provides public boot disk images for GPU and non-GPU VMs.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — only Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, plain or CUDA) public images are documented; no Windows Server image or licensing found.

macos.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — x86/GPU Linux cloud VMs on KVM-class hypervisor; no macOS/Apple-silicon VM offering exists.

self_host.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Nebius AI Cloud is a managed multi-tenant cloud platform; there is no self-hosted/on-prem distribution of Compute.

byoc.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Compute runs only in Nebius-owned regions/datacenters; no bring-your-own-cloud-account deployment model documented.

open_source.quote: Compute allows you to create and manage virtual machines (VMs). They are like your local machine, but in the cloud.
open_source.note: The Compute service itself is closed-source managed infrastructure; Nebius open-sources client tooling (CLI, SDKs, Terraform provider on GitHub) but not the core platform.

eu_data_residency.note: Multiple EU regions (eu-north1, eu-north2, eu-west1, eu-south1, eu-west2) are available for VM platforms, letting customers keep machines/data in the EU.

max_session_h.quote: A standalone VM can be regular or preemptible: regular VMs run until you stop them, while Compute may stop preemptible VMs at any time.
max_session_h.note: Regular (on-demand) VMs have no maximum runtime and run until the customer stops them; preemptible/spot VMs can be stopped by the provider at any time but that is capacity-based eviction, not a fixed session limit.
